newsitem.title: USA: FIA conference to focus on exchange cooperation.
newsitem.headline: FIA conference to focus on exchange cooperation.

text.p: The futures industry's annual conference this week will focus on cooperation between exchanges as the industry seeks to control cost pressures, industry officials said.
Among the hot topics concerning exchange cooperation are derivatives legislation, technology and common clearing, a Futures Industry Association (FIA) official said.

Recent developments concerning the Treasury amendment to the Commodity Exchange Act and an update on a task force investigating joint initiatives in Chicago will be presented when FIA hosts its 22nd annual conference in Boca Raton, Fla., Wednesday through Saturday.

"I think (cooperation) seems to be the wave of interest among the exchanges," said Leo Melamed, chairman emeritus of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and chairman of Sakura Dellsher. "Certainly it is true with the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and its undertaking with the Matif and the Paris bourse and with common clearing with the (Chicago) Board of Trade," he said.
For more than a year the futures industry has been watching negotiations between the two Chicago futures exchanges to find ways to cut costs and promote efficiencies.
Along those lines, the CBOT and the CME recently announced they would pursue a plan to consolidate the clearing functions of the two exchanges.
Melamed said he doubted whether the exchanges would announce any developments on common clearing at the conference, saying the project was "at the beginning point."
Reuters reported Monday that a study of the proposal to merge the two futures' exchanges clearing systems found that consolidating the hardware systems might not be economically feasible.

The CME also recently announced a planned software swap with French futures exchange Matif and several other exchanges. The CME and the New York Mercantile Exchange plan to adopt an electronic trading system developed by SBF-Paris Bourse and Matif SA, while the Paris markets will adopt a clearing system developed by the CME and NYMEX.
Futures industry sources said they also expected much interest from conference-goers in the latest legislative developments in derivatives regulation.
In late February, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that Congress had not authorized the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to regulate "off-exchange" trading in foreign currency options.
U.S. Senator Richard Lugar and others have introduced a bill to revise the Commodity Exchange Act, which governs U.S. futures trading.
